Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report for the Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery Program-for-Results reports a 31-Dec-2023 indicator where “0 percent of beneficiaries of the social programs receive digital G2P payments,” implying G2P digitization was not yet in active use for those programs at that time ([World Bank ISR – Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092325063510323/pdf/P176763-2035557c-fe0f-4162-a072-04b417dfb137.pdf)). Given evidence indicates no G2P digitization for social program beneficiaries (at least through 2023), score as No.
revision_notes: Re-fetched the cited World Bank ISR (same URL, now archived 23-Sep-2025, Seq 4): it does not contain the '0 percent of beneficiaries' quote used to justify the original score. Instead it shows a 'Digital Government to Person payments (Percentage) DLI' indicator with baseline 70% (Dec/2021) unchanged in the 'Actual (Current)' column, and a separate 'recipients of G2P/payers of P2G with access to an online platform' indicator at 0%, dated 31-Dec-2021 — an internally ambiguous pair of figures that does not clearly support either a firm 'No' or a firm 'Active Use' score, and the original supporting quote could not be verified in the document as it now stands. Searched further and found direct, dated, authoritative evidence: the Government of Benin's official portal (gouv.bj) confirms that the GBESSOKÉ productive social safety net programme (Ministry of Social Affairs and Microfinance) began monthly electronic cash transfers via mobile money on 18 September 2025, reaching 20,621 households (85% women) across 12 pilot communes, using dedicated SIM cards issued to beneficiaries specifically to receive 'transferts électroniques'; national scale-up to roughly 150,000 households across all 77 communes is planned. This is active government disbursement via a digital/mobile channel, but currently confined to a pilot covering a small share of eligible households, which corresponds to 'Limited Use' (2) rather than 'No' (1) on the variable's 0-3 scale. Score revised from 1 to 2; not a top-of-scale change so no human review flag required.
revised_comments: Benin uses digital channels for a subset of government-to-person disbursements, but on a limited scale. The GBESSOKÉ productive social safety nets programme, run by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Microfinance, began monthly electronic cash transfers by mobile money in September 2025, reaching 20,621 households (85% of them headed by women) across 12 pilot communes, with beneficiaries issued dedicated SIM cards to receive transfers. The programme is scheduled to scale up to around 150,000 households across all 77 communes. Other G2P flows, including elements of civil service pay, are reported by the World Bank to be partly digitised, though comprehensive system-wide figures are not publicly verified.
